collection: NERDC JSS 1 Physical and Health Education contact and non-contact sports
note: Original classroom knowledge and reasoning practice. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Identify contact as part of the intended action in wrestling.
questions.prompt: At a sports display, pupils watch wrestling and a lane swimming race. In which activity is physical contact with an opponent part of the normal contest?
questions.answer: Wrestling, where competitors use permitted holds to contest position.
questions.explanation: Wrestling involves deliberate physical interaction under rules. The swimmers race in separate lanes.
options: Swimming, because each competitor touches the pool wall.
Wrestling, where competitors use permitted holds to contest position.
Both, because both require physical effort.
Neither, because a referee or official can supervise both.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain how partner practice can develop cooperation and self-control.
questions.prompt: In a supervised judo lesson, two pupils take turns practising an exercise already demonstrated by the coach. One pupil notices that their partner needs more time before the next turn. Describe a cooperative response and explain how it shows self-control.
questions.answer: Pause, check that the partner is ready and wait for the coach’s signal before restarting. This shows control by delaying action until both pupils can take part as instructed.
questions.explanation: Partner practice gives pupils a reason to listen and adjust their own actions to the needs of another person.

markingGuide.description: Respects the partner’s pace and the coach’s direction.
Links the response to controlling one’s own actions.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Recognise a reason to pause a supervised contact-sport lesson.
questions.prompt: Before a school wrestling demonstration begins, two mats have separated and a gap lies inside the marked practice space. What should a pupil do?
questions.answer: Pause and tell the teacher so the mat area can be checked before practice.
questions.explanation: A gap interrupts the intended surface. Reporting it before practice lets the teacher correct the setup.
options: Step over the gap and start the demonstration.
Stand in the gap while another pupil practises.
Cover the gap with a school bag and carry on.
Pause and tell the teacher so the mat area can be checked before practice.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a lane race and an individual gymnastics routine are non-contact examples.
questions.prompt: A school programme includes a swim race in separate lanes and an individual gymnastics routine. Use the way each event is performed to explain why both are examples of non-contact sports.
questions.answer: Each swimmer races in an assigned lane without using physical contact to compete. Each gymnast performs their own routine without physical contact with an opponent.
questions.explanation: Non-contact here describes how competitors perform. They can compete for time or a score while performing separately.

markingGuide.description: Explains how separate lanes organise swimming without opponent contact.
Explains how the individual routine is performed without opponent contact.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Link different non-contact activities to movement abilities they practise.
questions.prompt: A pupil compares a familiar floor-balance exercise with a swimming lesson that practises timing the arms and legs together. Identify the main movement ability emphasised in each example and explain your choices.
questions.answer: The floor exercise emphasises balance because the pupil controls a steady position. The swimming lesson emphasises coordination because the pupil times different body movements together.
questions.explanation: Different practice tasks can emphasise different movement abilities. These examples isolate holding a position and timing movements together.

markingGuide.description: Identifies balance for the floor exercise.
Links balance to controlling a steady position.
Identifies coordination for the swimming lesson.
Links coordination to timing arm and leg actions.
